condition.narrative: Section I.A.1 of Schedule 2 of the Grant Agreement:The Recipient shall carry out the Project with due diligence and efficiency inconformity with appropriate administrative, financial, technical, environmental and social standards and practices and inaccordance with the provisions of this Agreement, the FMFA, the Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (“ESCP”) and the ProjectOperations Manual, and shall promptly provide the funds, facilities, services and other resources required for the Project.

Section I.A.2 (a) of Schedule 2 to the Grant Agreement: The Recipient shall establish, not later than one month after theSignature Date, and thereafter maintain throughout the period of the implementation of the Project, a coordination committee(“Project Coordination Committee”) with composition and terms of reference agreed by the Recipient and the Bank, to help provide,inter alia, the overall guidance for the Project, as further set out in the Project Operations Manual. The Recipient shallfacilitate the establishment and maintenance of the Project Coordination Committee.

Section I.B.1 of Schedule 2 to the Grant Agreement:The Recipient shall: (a) no later than one (1) month after theSignature Date, prepare and thereafter maintain, throughout the implementation of the Project, the Project Operations Manual, inform and substance satisfactory to the Bank, containing, inter alia, (i) a detailed description of the Project activities andinstitutional arrangements for their implementation; (ii) detailed terms of reference of the Project Coordination Committee and itsoperational arrangements; (iii) monitoring, evaluation, and reporting procedures for the Project, including third-party monitoringof project implementation; (iv) procedures, eligibility criteria, and mechanisms for Block Grants and targeting of Block GrantsService Providers, as agreed between the Bank and the Recipient in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement and the FMFA;(v) description of the package of Community Based Education services; and (vi) operational procedures and arrangements formonitoring compliance with Entry Criteria for Access; and (vii) implementation of environmental and social instruments referred toin the ESCP; and(b) carry out the Project in accordance with the provisions of the Project Operations Manual.

Section I.C.1 of Schedule 2 to the Grant Agreement:The Recipient shall, not later than one month after the Signature Date, andthereafter, on September 1, of each year during the implementation of the Project, or such later date as the Bank may agree inwriting prepare and furnish to the Bank for its approval, the Work Plan and Budget, covering activities to be implemented under theProject for the subsequent twelve (12) months, a proposed financing plan for expenditures required for such activities, and atimetable for their implementation. The Work Plan and Budget shall be reviewed on a six-monthly basis, and updated as required andagreed by the Recipient and the Bank.

Section I.D.1 of the Schedule 2 to the Grant Agreement:No later than one (1) month after the Signature Date, the Recipient shallhire and maintain throughout Project implementation, the Recipient's Third-Party Monitoring Agent, with qualifications, experienceand terms of reference satisfactory to the Bank, to be financed out of the proceeds of the Grant as set forth in the table underSection IV.A of Schedule 2 to this Agreement, to carry out Recipient's Third-Party Monitoring of the Project implementation,including, without limitation, periodic site visits, assessment of local context and conditions, verification of services volumeand quality, interviews, awareness raising, training, and preparation of reports.

Section I.G.1 of Schedule 2 to the Grant Agreement: The Recipient shall ensure that the Project is carried out in accordance withthe Environmental and Social Standards, in a manner acceptable to the Bank.

Public schools provided with the rehabilitation package (including WASH, boundary walls, classrooms, furniture, installation of solar panels) and/or disaster risk mitigation

comment.narrative: The school rehabilitation sub-component was discontinued due to delays from an ITA MoE directive requiring NGOs for civil work, contrary to project procedures and unacceptable to the Bank. Negotiations took substantial time delaying implementation. After agreeing to use private firms, UNICEF resumed activities but paused again in November 2025 when the MoE announced curriculum changes affecting donor projects. Ongoing delays made timely completion impossible, so it was decided to reallocate funds to other project activities through restructuring.

With the addition of the AF, the reach will extend to 3.2 million children.
